ov: The smallest member of the cockatoo family: a grey Australian parrot with a long tail and an expressive crest. Wild birds wander dry inland country in pairs or small flocks, always near water. It is one of the most commonly kept pet birds in the world.

why.p: One of the five most popular pet birds; an estimated 4.8 million US households keep them, though many are given up within about 1.5 years.
why.dm: Bred in captivity long enough for breeders to keep many colour mutations, such as cinnamon, silver and whiteface.

len: 30–33 cm, about half of it tail
rg: Mainland Australia, mostly in arid or semi-arid country but always near water. It is largely nomadic, moving to wherever food and water are.
df: Seeds, especially acacia, wheat, sunflower and sorghum. To many farmers' dismay, it often eats their crops.

cf.tip: The cockatiel is the smallest cockatoo, 30–33 cm long, and unlike most cockatoos its tail makes up about half its length.

fx: Pet cockatiels learn words and copy household sounds, including alarm clocks and phones.
The average life is 12–15 years, but a well-kept pet can live 16–25, and one reached 36.
